idea: Singapore family office market entry advisory for UK managers
buyer: UK boutique asset managers wanting Asian capital
pain: Singapore family office capital is growing and UK managers cannot access it
v1: A market map and introduction plan for one manager
channel: Her Singapore contacts plus UK fund network
verdict: Both ends warm-ish and a real capital flow, but capital introduction is regulated territory.

why.distribution: UK managers are her network; Singapore family offices are scattered contacts requiring development.
why.demand: UK boutiques actively want Asian capital and do pay placement and consulting fees.
why.fmf: She understands managers and allocators but has no capital-raising track record.
why.revenue_structure: Engagement plus retainer while the mandate runs.
why.tailwind: Singapore family office formation is one of the strongest wealth trends globally.
why.ceiling: £20k x 10 managers = £200k, but ten simultaneous mandates is beyond solo capacity.

ceiling_arithmetic: £20k x 10 manager engagements = £200k gross less ~£20k travel = £180k. Ten mandates is beyond solo delivery; realistic is 3-4 = £48-64k net.
carries: Genuinely strong tailwind and a plausible position between two groups she can reach.
kills: Capital introduction is regulated activity in most forms, and she has no fundraising track record.
test: Take regulatory advice first, then ask two UK managers what they would pay for Asian capital access.
test_pass: A structure outside the perimeter exists and a manager will pay for it.
test_fail: It requires authorisation or managers only pay on success.
